ai.description: This 15 cm lizard has a bronze-brown body with a prominent pale dorsolateral stripe bordered by dark edges. It features a wedge-shaped snout and smooth, overlapping scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eutropis dissimilis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, narrow, pale vertebral stripe bordered by dark brown or blackish longitudinal bands along its back.
ai.habitat: *Eutropis dissimilis* inhabits open grasslands, scrublands, and agricultural fields across the Indian subcontinent, typically at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Striped Grass Mabuya is a diurnal lizard that actively hunts for small insects among leaf litter and grasses, often basking in sunlight to regulate its body temperature.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eutropis dissimilis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–8 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eutropis dissimilis* occurs across northern and central India, ranging from the Himalayan foothills to the Deccan Plateau, typically at low to moderate elevations.
